findings.text: §15 fixes the bug ("a host's own follower reads as hand-armed") with a new parent-process identity check, but the machinery for both halves of that check already exists and §15 cites none of it. Reading an ancestor's identity as a `crew host` is already `_current_and_ancestor_argvs` (`reckon/crew/dispatch_watch.py:89`), which walks `/proc/<pid>/cmdline` up the ancestor chain nearest-first, together with `_process_start_time` (`reckon/crew/dispatch_watch.py:396`, imported at `:32`) — both in a file §15 already lists among its write paths. The process that armed the follower is already recorded and survives the in-place reload that caused the incident: the host stamps `RECKON_FOLLOWER_OWNER` with its own pid when it spawns each child (`environ[_FOLLOWER_OWNER_ENV] = _format_follower_owner((os.getpid(), ...))`, `reckon/crew/session_host.py:409`), read by `follower_owner()` (`reckon/crew/runs.py:3060`, fixed once at `:3024`–`3032` per the comment at `:3002`–`3013`). That env predates the reverted child marker, so a follower from an old host — the exact population §15 exists for — carries it. Census of same-fact signals §15 must reconcile, none cited: the marker `CHILD_ENV` (fast path, §15); the owner env `RECKON_FOLLOWER_OWNER` (already the host pid for a host child, `reckon/crew/runs.py:3002`, `reckon/crew/session_host.py:409`); the host's own child census `children[]` (`reckon/crew/session_host.py:310`–`325`) read by `_session_host_runs_follower` (`reckon/crew/dispatch_watch.py:477`). §15 adds a third signal where the owner env already answers the question without a `/proc` walk

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — §15 adds no new module; it is one predicate (is my parent a crew host) split policy-versus-transport across two existing modules, which is depth rather than added surface.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: pass — §15's stated aim, "one request writer in `reckon/crew/dispatch_watch.py`", consolidates the two request-line writers rather than adding one, and the parent check names no state reader it forks.

rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — §15's parent-process child check is proposed without a search of the ancestor-/owner-identity machinery already present in its own write paths (`_current_and_ancestor_argvs` at `reckon/crew/dispatch_watch.py:89`, the follower owner env at `reckon/crew/runs.py:3002`–`3013`, the host census at `reckon/crew/session_host.py:310`–`325`).
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the parent check extends the existing child-detection (the marker) instead of wrapping a parallel subsystem, and §15 states in its own text why the marker cannot be trusted alone (hosts started before it carried no marker, so a reloaded child read as hand-armed).
